title: Dynamically frozen long-distance entanglement via non-Hermitian PT-symmetric systems
authors: Sejal Ahuja, Keshav Das Agarwal, Aditi Sen De
abstract: In distributed quantum networks, interacting spin systems can mediate the generation of highly entangled links between distant nodes. We investigate the role of effective parity-time (PT)-symmetric non-Hermitian spin-1/2 bulks weakly coupled to two quantum links, obtained due to the environmental interactions affecting both the bulk and the links. Focusing on effective non-Hermitian nearest-neighbor (NN) Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) models, we analyze how non-Hermiticity influences the dynamical formation of long-distance entanglement (LDE). For a paradigmatic model consisting of a quantum XX bulk subjected to imaginary staggered magnetic fields, we analytically determine the exceptional points arising from the resulting bulk-mediated interactions between the links. Combining analytical and numerical methods, we demonstrate that an initially fully separable state can dynamically evolve into highly entangled link states near these exceptional points in the broken regime. Further, after optimizing over time and system parameters, near-unit time-averaged entanglement between the links emerges under weak imaginary magnetic fields and bulk-link couplings, which cannot be attained in the corresponding Hermitian systems. Moreover, the non-Hermitian dynamics exhibit a freezing of high entanglement in the vicinity of exceptional points, a feature absent in Hermitian counterparts. We also identify regimes of long-range interaction strengths that yield a higher time-averaged entanglement than the corresponding NN models. Furthermore, we establish that LDE persists in the stationary regime, highlighting the promise of engineered non-Hermitian dynamics for realizing robust and frozen entangled links in quantum networks.
summary: This paper demonstrates that incorporating non-Hermititian physics into spin chain models can dramatically enhance the generation and stabilization of long-distance entanglement in quantum networks. By analyzing dynamics near exceptional points, the authors show that these engineered systems achieve higher, more robust levels of entanglement than their Hermitian counterparts.
main_problem: The study investigates how non-Hermitian dynamics can dynamically generate and stabilize long-distance entanglement (LDE) between distant nodes in quantum networks, comparing this to standard Hermitian evolution.
main_result: Non-Hermitian dynamics near exceptional points allow for the emergence of near-unit time-averaged entanglement that cannot be achieved by corresponding Hermitian systems. Furthermore, LDE persists robustly even in the stationary regime.
method: The analysis combines analytical techniques (like determining exceptional points) with numerical simulations to track entanglement evolution over time and across parameter space.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as interacting spin-1/2 bulks weakly coupled to two quantum links, analyzed using an effective non-Hermitian nearest-neighbor Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model derived from open quantum system dynamics.
key_observables: Long-distance entanglement ($\mathcal{E}_{\ell_1\ell_2}$), time-averaged link entanglement ($E_{	ext{avg}}^{\ell_1\ell_2}$), and the location of exceptional points (EPs).
important_parameters: Weak coupling strength ($\lambda$), imaginary magnetic fields ($h'$), system size ($N$), and the SSH model parameter $\delta$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on deriving effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonians from open quantum systems (e.g., via GKLS master equation) and assumes weak coupling regimes for perturbative calculations.
figures_summary: Figures compare entanglement dynamics in the broken vs. unbroken regimes, show how LDE depends on system size $N$ and interaction range ($\alpha$), and map out high-entanglement regions near exceptional point lines in parameter space.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the role of non-Hermiticity by comparing dynamic entanglement generation across different SSH model parameters ($\delta$) and coupling strengths, culminating in a comparison between stationary and time-averaged entanglement results.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses engineered quantum networks using non-Hermitian physics, providing concrete mechanisms (EPs, broken phase) to enhance robust quantum correlations beyond what is possible with standard unitary models.

FIG. 3. Time-averaged entanglement between the links Eavg ℓ1ℓ2: Exceptional points are special. Time-averaged LDE Eavg ℓ1ℓ2 of the SSH model in the parameter space (h, λ) (abscissa, ordinate) for (a) δ = 0.8 and (b) δ = 1.2, with N = 16. The exceptional points are represented by dashed-dot lines, which segregate the unbroken (U) and broken (B) phases. High LDE (> 0.8) (pink colored regions) can be obtained near the exceptional lines of the model, especially for δ ≥1 (see Theorem 2, for δ = 1). The initial state of the bulk and link system is |Ψ(0)⟩= |1⟩. All the axes are dimensionless.

FIG. 2. Comparison between long-distance entanglement Eℓ1ℓ2 of unbroken and broken regimes of the non-Hermitian SSH model. Eℓ1ℓ2 (ordinate) vs time (abscissa) for δ = 1.2 where (a) belongs to the broken regime and (b) to unbroken regime. The model fa- cilitates long-distance entanglement creation in both regimes, with frozen entangled links in the broken regimes for a long period of time (a). However, the entanglement in the unbroken regime fluctu- ates, and the freezing periods are shorter. The system is initialized as |Ψ(0)⟩= |1⟩⊗|0⟩⊗N−1 with the system-size N = 16. All the axes are dimensionless.

FIG. 4. Scaling of LDE with system-size: Comparison between non-Hermitian and Hermitian LDE generation. The entangle- ment Eavg,X max (ordinate), averaged over time and maximized over the (h, λ)-plane with respect to the system-size N (abscissa) for (a) non- Hermitian (X=nH) and (b) the Hermitian (X=H) models. Different lines denote different δ values of the SSH model. Eavg,X max decays slowly when δ ≈1, whereas the LDE decays quickly with system- size N when δ ̸= 1 and high N, highlighting the significance of XX model. (Inset) When entanglement is close to unity (Eavg,nH max < 0.9), the scaling exponents are found for δ = 0.9, 1.0 and 1.1. All the axes are dimensionless.

FIG. 6. Long-distance entangled links in a stationary state. The variation of entanglement between the links ˜Eℓ1ℓ2 in the (h, λ)- plane is presented when the system reaches the stationary state for (a) δ = 0.75 and (b) δ = 1.25, with system-size N = 10. The broken (B) and unbroken (U) regimes are separated by the dashed-dot lines. High entanglement between the links (ℓ1, ℓ2) is produced close to the exceptional line with pink colored regions indicating ˜Eℓ1ℓ2 ≥0.95. All the axes are dimensionless.
